summary.text: A 49-year-old Chinese woman with no past medical history or records suggesting bleeding diathesis presented to the emergency department with a four-day history of constant abdominal pain, non-bloody vomiting, diarrhea and persistent gross hematuria. She was afebrile, with heart rate 103 beats per minute, blood pressure 88/57 mmHg, pallor and right iliac fossa tenderness without guarding or rebound.

Point-of-care ultrasound showed free fluid. Blood investigations showed anemia, a normal platelet count and profound coagulopathy with prothrombin time above 180 seconds and warfarin-like deficiency of factors II, VII, IX and X. CT of the abdomen and pelvis showed large-volume hemoperitoneum, with a ruptured right corpus luteal cyst the likely source. Blood toxicology confirmed bromadiolone poisoning.

She received one unit each of red blood cells and fresh frozen plasma before transfer to a tertiary hospital. About 20 hours after admission she underwent diagnostic laparoscopy, right cystectomy and peritoneal washout, after fresh frozen plasma, cryoprecipitate and intravenous vitamin K. Postoperatively she received intravenous vitamin K, then oral vitamin K from postoperative day 6, with ongoing supportive transfusions and replacement.

She was admitted for a total of 10 days and discharged well on a tapering course of oral vitamin K. Follow-up tests two weeks after discharge showed a normal coagulation profile, and the latest tests, about two months after initial presentation, showed platelet count 242 x 10^(9)/L, PT 10.5 seconds and INR 1.0 before she was lost to follow-up.
